chunks: From him, from several of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sama'ah, who said:

I asked him about the woman who performs khal' (redeems herself from divorce). He said: It is not permissible for her husband to grant her khal' until she says: 'I will not be dutiful to you with an oath, and I will not establish God's boundaries within you, and I will not perform the ritual bath for you from major impurity, and I will surely bed your bed, and I will surely bring into your house whom you dislike, without you knowing this.' And he does not speak, and she is the one who says this. When she performs khal', she becomes irrevocably divorced (bain), and he has the right to take from her wealth whatever he can manage, but he does not have the right to take from the mubari'ah (the compensation amount) more than what he had given her.

key_terms.المختلعة: The woman who performs khal' (redeems herself)
key_terms.لا أبر لك قسما: I will not be dutiful to you with an oath (declaration of disobedience)

ai.seo_question: What are the conditions for a valid khal' divorce and the husband's financial rights in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Isfahani’s al-Istibsar clarifies the Shia juristic view that khal' requires the wife to explicitly declare her intent to disobey marital duties, distinguishing it from mutual consent. It establishes that while the husband may reclaim his mahr or compensation, he cannot claim more than what he originally provided, ensuring financial equity in the dissolution.
